sourceEnglish.title: The Guide Moves the Bus Up: Settle the Finca Order
sourceEnglish.objective: Recount what the group ordered and paid, count items fast, and settle the bill before the bus leaves.
sourceEnglish.speaking: You are the group's organizer, and the AI is Marleny, the cook at a coffee-farm breakfast near Salento: recount what the group ordered and who paid using the preterite (pedimos, pagaron), count what's still owed with faltan + numbers, and settle the bill before the bus leaves.
englishWordAnchors: the scrambled eggs with tomato and onion
We ordered 7 arepas with cheese and 9 small black coffees.
Doña Marleny, 4 have already paid in cash.
There are still 3 black coffees and 2 aguapanelas to pay for.
Andrés said the minibus leaves in 10 minutes.
Guys, who ordered the scrambled eggs with tomato and onion?
Could you confirm how much of the balance is left, please?
Can I pay you by bank transfer or only in cash?
I'll pay what's left and sort it out with them later.
englishGrammarExamples: We ordered 7 arepas, and 4 people already paid.
Marleny served 2 calentados that nobody wrote down in the notebook.
englishReading: At 7:30, Emma's group finished breakfast at a coffee farm near Salento.
Suddenly, the guide Andrés announced that they moved the departure up to 7:45 because of a landslide on the road.
Emma, the organizer, went to the kitchen and told the cook: Andrés said the minibus leaves in 10 minutes.
Doña Marleny opened the notebook where she wrote down the group's orders that morning.
Emma: We ordered 7 arepas with cheese and 9 small black coffees.
Marleny: Yes, and also 2 aguapanelas for Priya's kids.
Emma: Doña Marleny, 4 have already paid in cash.
Marleny: Okay, but I also served 2 calentados that nobody wrote down in the notebook.
Emma asked her companions: Guys, who ordered the scrambled eggs with tomato and onion?
Tom and Priya raised their hands, and Tom admitted that he also ate a calentado with farmer's cheese.
Marleny added it up quickly with her pencil and said: There are still 3 black coffees and 2 aguapanelas to pay for.
Emma: Could you confirm how much of the balance is left, please?
Marleny: The outstanding balance is 64 thousand pesos, with the scrambled eggs and the 2 calentados.
Emma only had large 100 thousand-peso bills, and Marleny didn't have change so early.
Emma: Can I pay you by bank transfer or only in cash?
Marleny answered that she does accept transfers through Nequi and showed her the number stuck on the wall.
Emma told her: I'll pay what's left and sort it out with them later.
Emma made the transfer of 64 thousand pesos, showed her the proof of payment, and ran to the minibus just in time.

lessons.title: Settle a group breakfast bill before departure
lessons.objective: Recount the group's orders and recorded payments, check the remaining balance with staff, and settle it before the shuttle departs.
lessons.focus: ～を注文しました and ～が支払いました recount completed actions; まだ～が残っています tracks what remains. The English source's pesos, Nequi transfer and Colombian foods are provenance, not Japanese learner copy. Verify each charge and the shop's accepted payment method before paying.
lessons.scene: A group organizer checks a rural café's order ledger as an earlier shuttle departure approaches.

cards.ja: いくら残っていますか

reader.speaker: Guide
reader.ja: 送迎車の出発が早まりました。あと十分です。
reader.en: The shuttle departure has moved up. We have ten minutes.

reader.speaker: Organizer
reader.ja: 注文票と支払いを一緒に確認してもいいですか。
reader.en: May we check the order sheet and payments together?

reader.speaker: Cook
reader.ja: はい。コーヒーを九杯と朝食を七人分記録しています。
reader.en: Yes. I recorded nine coffees and seven breakfasts.

reader.speaker: Organizer
reader.ja: 四人はもう現金で支払いました。
reader.en: Four people have already paid in cash.

reader.speaker: Cook
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。まだ二人分の朝食代が残っています。
reader.en: Thank you. Payment for two breakfasts still remains.

reader.speaker: Organizer
reader.ja: 追加の注文があったか、皆に確認します。
reader.en: I will ask everyone whether there were extra orders.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 私がコーヒーを一杯追加しました。まだ払っていません。
reader.en: I ordered one extra coffee. I have not paid for it yet.

reader.speaker: Organizer
reader.ja: 合計と残額をもう一度教えていただけますか。
reader.en: Could you tell me the total and remaining balance again?

reader.speaker: Cook
reader.ja: こちらが内訳です。お支払いは現金かカードです。
reader.en: Here is the itemized bill. You can pay with cash or card.

reader.speaker: Organizer
reader.ja: 内訳を確認しました。カードで残りを支払い、領収書を受け取ります。
reader.en: I checked the itemization. I will pay the rest by card and take the receipt.

speaking.opening: 出発前に、注文票と未払いの金額を確認できますか。
speaking.goal: Recount ordered and paid items, ask for an itemized remaining balance, and confirm the accepted payment method before settling.
speaking.closure: Check the final receipt and avoid declaring a debt paid before staff confirms the payment.

modes.see: Read the itemized-bill dialogue with English support.
modes.recall: Recall the ordered, paid and remaining counts.
modes.hear: Hear past-tense order and payment statements.
modes.type: Type a remaining-balance question with kana help.
modes.say: Reconcile the group order with staff before departure.
modes.write: Write an itemized payment summary and confirmation request.

sourceEnglish.title: Decline the Offer to Scrape the Almonds Off
sourceEnglish.objective: Refuse a well-meant but unsafe offer for an allergic friend and ask for a safe option or none at all.
sourceEnglish.speaking: You are with your friend Kenji, who has a tree-nut allergy, and the AI is Jordi, a server at a granja in Gràcia: thank him warmly but turn down his offer with negative commands like no la raspes and no recomiendo que + subjunctive, then ask for a safe option or nothing at all.
englishWordAnchors: the hot chocolate with whipped cream
Thanks, Jordi, but please don't scrape it.
I really appreciate it, honestly, you're very kind.
He has a severe tree-nut allergy.
I don't recommend Kenji try it, even if you remove the almonds.
Kenji, don't eat it; there are bits left in the dough.
Don't push it, Kenji; it's not worth the risk.
Do you have anything packaged, with the allergen label?
If there's no safe option, he'd rather not eat anything.
englishGrammarExamples: Please don't scrape it; the almonds leave bits behind.
I don't recommend that Kenji try anything from the bakery kitchen without a label.
englishReading: Ana and her friend Kenji are having breakfast on a Saturday at a traditional café in the Gràcia neighborhood, in Barcelona.
Kenji orders a hot chocolate with whipped cream, and Jordi, the server, recommends the house coca to them, fresh out of the oven.
Ana looks at the coca and sees that the whole surface is covered in almonds.
Ana points to Kenji and explains to Jordi: He has a severe tree-nut allergy.
Jordi, with great kindness, offers to scrape the almonds off a slice for Kenji.
Ana: I really appreciate it, honestly, you're very kind.
Ana: Thanks, Jordi, but please don't scrape it.
Ana: I don't recommend Kenji try it, even if you remove the almonds.
Jordi admits that in the bakery kitchen they make the dough on the same table where they work with almonds all day.
Kenji hesitates and says that a small piece isn't going to hurt him.
Ana: Kenji, don't eat it; there are bits left in the dough.
Ana: Don't push it, Kenji; it's not worth the risk.
Kenji remembers that last year he had anaphylaxis from a piece of nougat.
He carries his antihistamine and his auto-injector, as his doctor told him, and Ana knows that, if there are symptoms, the auto-injector is used and 112 is called.
Ana: Do you have anything packaged, with the allergen label?
Jordi brings a packaged product, but the label says it may contain traces of tree nuts.
Ana: If there's no safe option, he'd rather not eat anything.

Jordi checks the allergen chart and confirms that the hot chocolate has no tree nuts among its ingredients; Ana asks whether it is prepared with clean utensils, and Kenji decides to order it only if the kitchen confirms.

lessons.title: Decline removal of nuts from a prepared pastry
lessons.objective: Politely decline an offer to remove nuts from a prepared pastry for a friend with a tree-nut allergy, and ask about a verifiable alternative or choose nothing.
lessons.focus: お気持ちはありがたいですが acknowledges kindness before declining; 取り除かないでください is a direct negative request. 木の実アレルギー and アナフィラキシー name the source's clinical terms; 表面 and 生地 distinguish the visible topping from the pastry itself.
lessons.scene: At a bakery café, a server offers to remove almond pieces from a pastry; the guests decline and ask for current labeling and preparation information.

cards.ja: お気持ちはありがたいですが
アドレナリン自己注射器

reader.speaker: Server
reader.ja: この菓子パンはいかがですか。アーモンドが上にのっています。
reader.en: How about this pastry? It has almonds on top.

reader.speaker: Guest
reader.ja: 友人は木の実にアレルギーがあります。
reader.en: My friend has a tree-nut allergy.

reader.speaker: Server
reader.ja: 上のアーモンドを取り除きましょうか。
reader.en: Shall I remove the almonds on top?

reader.speaker: Guest
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。でも、アーモンドを取り除かないでください。
reader.en: Thank you, but please don't scrape off the almonds.

reader.speaker: Guest
reader.ja: 見える分を取り除くだけでは、原材料や混入を確認できません。
reader.en: Removing the visible pieces does not verify the ingredients or possible cross-contact.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 原材料表示のある別の商品はありますか。
reader.en: Do you have another product with an ingredient label?

reader.speaker: Server
reader.ja: こちらは包装されていますが、製造場所の情報も確認します。
reader.en: This one is packaged, but I will check the production information too.

reader.speaker: Guest
reader.ja: 確認できない場合は、何も注文しません。
reader.en: If it cannot be verified, we will not order food.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 飲み物も調理方法を確認してから決めます。
reader.en: I will decide about a drink only after checking how it is prepared.

reader.speaker: Server
reader.ja: 分かりました。確認できた情報だけをお伝えします。
reader.en: Understood. I will tell you only what we can verify.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 以前、木の実でアナフィラキシーを起こしたことがあります。
reader.en: I have had anaphylaxis from tree nuts before.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 医師の指示で、抗ヒスタミン薬とアドレナリン自己注射器を持っています。
reader.en: I carry an antihistamine and an epinephrine auto-injector as my doctor instructed.

speaking.opening: 友人は木の実にアレルギーがあります。アーモンドを取り除くだけでは注文できません。
speaking.goal: Thank the server, decline scraping almonds off the pastry, explain the friend's tree-nut allergy and past anaphylaxis, and ask about another item.
speaking.closure: End by restating the friend's decision about the offered food.

modes.see: Read a polite refusal scene with aligned English.
modes.recall: Recall why visible nut removal is insufficient.
modes.hear: Hear a warm acknowledgement followed by a clear refusal.
modes.type: Type a refusal with kana support.
modes.say: Tell the server about the tree-nut allergy and past anaphylaxis; decline scraping off almonds and ask about another item.
modes.write: Write a concise request for current ingredient and preparation details.

sourceEnglish.title: Give Honest Feedback to a New Café Owner
sourceEnglish.objective: Give specific, kind feedback on coffee and menu clarity and make two concrete recommendations.
sourceEnglish.speaking: You are a customer, and the AI is Camila, the new café owner in Barrio Italia: give honest, kind feedback on the cortado and the chalkboard menu, and make two concrete recommendations using le recomiendo que and ojalá que with the present subjunctive.
englishWordAnchors: If you want my honest opinion, the cortado arrived a bit cold.
I recommend that you warm the cups before serving.
I hope the cortado comes out a little hotter.
I suggest you separate the coffees from the sweets by category.
It's better if you write the prices in bigger letters.
I loved the kuchen, it was truly delicious.
I hope what I'm saying doesn't bother you.
I really hope things go great with the café, Camila.
englishGrammarExamples: I recommend that you put the prices next to each coffee.
I hope the milk comes out hotter tomorrow.
englishReading: Daniel, a Canadian traveler, has a cortado and eats a raspberry kuchen at Camila's new café in Barrio Italia.
Camila opened the place two weeks ago and asks Daniel for his honest opinion about the coffee and the menu.
Daniel: If you want my honest opinion, the cortado arrived a bit cold.
Daniel: The crema looked very nice, but the steamed milk arrived lukewarm.
Camila explains that the espresso machine is new and that she is still learning to control the temperature.
She says that she adjusts the grinder every morning so that the espresso comes out well.
Daniel notices that the cup warmer is turned off on top of the machine.
Daniel: I recommend that you warm the cups before serving.
Daniel: I hope the cortado comes out a little hotter.
Then Daniel looks at the menu board, written in white chalk, and finds it confusing.
Daniel: The handwriting is very small and the prices are not readable from the register.
Daniel: I suggest you separate the coffees from the sweets by category.
Daniel: It's better if you write the prices in bigger letters.
Camila: You're right, the first impression is very important in a new place.
Daniel: I hope what I'm saying doesn't bother you.
Camila: Not at all, I really appreciate the suggestion.
Daniel: I loved the kuchen, it was truly delicious.
Daniel: I really hope things go great with the café, Camila.

lessons.title: Give kind, specific feedback to a café owner
lessons.objective: Tell a café owner what worked, explain two observable problems with the coffee and menu, and offer two concrete suggestions without claiming technical certainty.
lessons.focus: 少し～でした gives measured feedback; ～すると見やすいと思います and ～してはいかがですか make suggestions. Describe the served drink and readable prices rather than diagnosing the espresso machine or promising that a technical adjustment will fix the result.
lessons.scene: A regular customer gives a new café owner courteous feedback about a lukewarm drink and hard-to-read menu board.

reader.speaker: Owner
reader.ja: 新しい店の感想を聞かせていただけますか。
reader.en: Could you tell me what you thought of the new café?

reader.speaker: Customer
reader.ja: ケーキはおいしかったです。飲み物とメニューについて二つ提案があります。
reader.en: The cake was delicious. I have two suggestions about the drink and menu.

reader.speaker: Owner
reader.ja: ぜひ教えてください。
reader.en: Please tell me.

reader.speaker: Customer
reader.ja: 今日のカフェオレは、私には少しぬるく感じました。
reader.en: Today's café au lait felt a little lukewarm to me.

reader.speaker: Customer
reader.ja: 提供する前に温度を確認してはいかがですか。
reader.en: How about checking the temperature before serving it?

reader.speaker: Owner
reader.ja: 分かりました。店の手順を見直してみます。
reader.en: I see. I will review our shop procedure.

reader.speaker: Customer
reader.ja: それから、レジからはメニュー板の値段が読みにくかったです。
reader.en: Also, the menu-board prices were hard to read from the register.

reader.speaker: Customer
reader.ja: 飲み物と甘い物を分けて、値段を大きく書くと見やすいと思います。
reader.en: I think separating drinks and sweets and writing prices larger would make it easier to read.

reader.speaker: Owner
reader.ja: 具体的な提案をありがとうございます。
reader.en: Thank you for the specific suggestions.

reader.speaker: Customer
reader.ja: こちらこそ。新しいお店を応援しています。
reader.en: Thank you. I am rooting for your new café.

speaking.opening: ケーキはおいしかったです。飲み物とメニューについて、少し感想をお伝えしてもいいですか。
speaking.goal: Praise one thing, identify two observable issues, and offer two respectful, concrete suggestions.
speaking.closure: Leave the owner room to choose how to respond; avoid asserting a technical cause you did not verify.
